terminal_bridge:
A single model invocation produces exactly one unprivileged, stochastic candidate sequence. When that sequence is ambiguous, incomplete, or fails host-side verification, simply re-issuing the prompt with identical parameters compounds failure modes. In classical systems design, when a single speculative operation yields low confidence, the architecture introduces branching, speculative execution, or multi-path verification. Chapter 03 examines how the runtime allocates additional inference-time compute—structuring sequential deliberation, tree search, and verification oracles—to transform stochastic candidate proposals into dependable systems outcomes before touching external environment state.

:::
cumulative_ledger: Section 2.1 (The Model Invocation Boundary): The foundation model is an unprivileged inference engine that maps staged token sequences to candidate probability distributions; the host agent runtime is the authoritative supervisor that owns context staging, execution limits, and action verification.

Section 2.2 (Discrete Tokenization and Sequence Representation): A tokenizer is a statistical byte serializer between strings and integer indices; its subwords clash with programming language ASTs and introduce a significant serialization tax on structured tool calls.

Section 2.3 (Autoregressive Generation and the Serving Loop): Generating a sequence requires an iterative serving loop that repeatedly evaluates the model forward pass and samples a token, creating an irreducibly serial causal dependency along one output path.

Section 2.4 (Prefill, Decode, and Accelerator Hardware Physics): Model invocation latency is split between compute-bound prompt prefill and memory-bandwidth-bound token decode; single-batch agent trajectories are physically bounded by the HBM parameter shuttle.

Section 2.5 (Constraining the Output: Grammar-Guided Decoding): Grammar-constrained decoding enforces structural syntax via decode-time logit masking on the accelerator, guaranteeing valid format while leaving semantic truth completely unverified.

Section 2.6 (The Invocation Contract and Status Envelopes): Robust agent systems govern model calls through a typed RPC contract with explicit token and latency ceilings, streaming early cancellation, and a normalized status envelope.

Section 2.7 (Verification Boundaries: Likelihood Versus Operational Truth): Sequence likelihood does not establish operational correctness; model outputs are unverified hypotheses requiring host validation before mutating state.

Section 2.8 (Systems Benchmarking of Invocation Interfaces): Invocation interfaces must be evaluated by downstream verified task success under equal resource budgets, not by superficial fluency or parsing speed.
